title: Chapter 220: Shadowing
html:
“Boss! Mr. Han! Look behind you!” Xiao Du ran back to the group, gasping for breath, his face drained of color.

“Behind us?” Guo Miao glanced back, but the long corridor appeared empty.

“The mannequins! They’re coming after us!” Xiao Du’s shout brought the group to another halt several meters inside the Third Sick Hall.

“Are you sure you’re not mistaken?” Song An asked quietly, edging closer to Guo Miao.

“I’m sure! They really moved!” Xiao Du fought to catch his breath. “Come take a look for yourself. Those mannequins were at the far end of the left corridor before, right? Now they’ve reached the space between the two scenarios!”

“Don’t panic,” Han Qiuming said calmly. “I saw something similar in a Japanese Haunted House three years ago. It had a doll-themed scenario. The smaller dolls contained mechanisms that let them move and change their facial expressions. Of the larger dolls, only four-fifths were props; the rest were played by actors.”

“So some of those mannequins are people?” Mr. Han’s explanation only confused Xiao Du and left him even more unsettled.

“I noticed the mannequins as soon as we came in.” Han Qiuming crossed his arms over his chest. “They’re life-sized, as though modeled on actual people. You have to understand—even at Tian Teng Medical School, the mannequins we use as ordinary props have obvious flaws. Custom-made mannequins are simply too expensive. A single one can cost around thirty thousand yuan and requires a master dollmaker to produce. An ordinary Haunted House couldn’t afford them.”

“Then why would this Haunted House spend so much on these mannequins?” Ye Xiaoxin continued writing in her notebook, though no one knew what she was recording.

“Simple. It proves that the mannequins are one of this Haunted House’s main scare elements.” Han Qiuming stroked his chin, his gaze settling on Ye Xiaoxin. “Mixing actors in among the mannequins can produce startling results—just look at what happened to Xiao Du. It seemed as if the mannequins had moved on their own, but the ones that moved were actually actors. If we hid in the dark and watched, we might even catch them in motion.”

Song An nodded. “Mr. Han has a point. We used a similar trick at Tian Teng Medical School last year, but our mannequins looked too fake. Visitors spotted the actors immediately.”

“That must be it.” Color returned to Xiao Du’s face. “They really spooked me just now. Those mannequins look so lifelike that I thought they could move on their own.”

“You know that’s impossible,” Mr. Han said confidently, secure in his reasoning. “If we weren’t under a time limit, I’d hide in this room and record the Haunted House actors moving the mannequins so you could see for yourself.”

“All right, let’s keep moving. We still need to find the tape recorder.” Guo Miao sensed that things were not so simple, but he had no evidence with which to challenge Mr. Han.

“Old Guo, there are two things we need to keep in mind about that recorder.” Mr. Han might have claimed not to be afraid, but he was clearly on high alert. “That Chen fellow told us our recorder was hidden here, so he must have set traps around it.”

“I know.” Guo Miao pressed on. Mattresses lay scattered everywhere, and stepping on them felt disturbingly like treading on bundles of hair.

“That’s only the first thing. There’s something else. Don’t you find the rules he set rather strange?”

“How so?”

“Finding the tape recorder won’t clear the scenario. We have to bring it out of the Third Sick Hall to end the game.”

“But the recorder belongs to us. Isn’t it only natural that we take it with us?” Xiao Du interjected.

“You’ve underestimated the boss’s cunning.” Han Qiuming took out a cloth and wiped his thick lenses. “The recorder is probably linked to some mechanism in this place. In other words, the moment we find it, the real scares will begin. Until then, we should be safe.”

“That sounds reasonable, but there’s no guarantee you’re right.” Song An was the largest of them, yet also one of the most timid.

“In any case, I see no reason for us to be afraid. Our priority should be learning the layout and memorizing our route. This is an open-ended scenario, so the environment is bound to be complicated. If we retrace our steps, we’ll be able to escape as quickly as possible once we find the recorder and the actors begin moving in earnest.” Han Qiuming concluded his analysis. Whether or not the others believed him was unclear, but he certainly believed himself.

“You have a point. Haunted Houses still rely on actors to scare people. As long as we stay calm and don’t frighten ourselves, we should be fine.” Ye Xiaoxin slipped the notebook into her pocket.

Emboldened by Ye Xiaoxin’s approval, Han Qiuming felt his fear slowly recede. He was about to quicken his pace and join her when someone tugged on his shirt. He turned to find the youngest and most tactless member of the group, Du Chaojin.

“Mr. Han, look.” Everyone turned toward the entrance to the Third Sick Hall. A female mannequin in a school uniform stood in its center, head bowed and limbs twisted at slight angles.

While they had been busy theorizing, the mannequins had drawn closer.

“This is nothing unusual—just the most basic kind of psychological trick. That Chen fellow is probably hiding in the control room, directing the actors. He wants these advancing mannequins to put pressure on us and make us panic.”

Han Qiuming tried to rationalize everything. “At the end of the day, it’s all fake. I used something similar a few years ago. Don’t worry—the mannequins won’t dare come within five meters of us. That’s the safe distance. If they get any closer, the actors will have trouble controlling them convincingly. I stake my decade of experience on it.”

Ignoring Xiao Du, he hurried to Ye Xiaoxin’s side and began critiquing the Haunted House’s various decorations.

“What a guy.” Guo Miao sighed, then addressed the group. “Everyone stay close to me. Don’t touch anything in the corridor, and don’t enter a sickroom alone.”

“Okay.” Xiao Du brought up the rear, unaware that whenever he moved, the mannequins beyond the entrance moved as well.
